body.html: Pacinn Narathiwat is a new hotel that opened in 2025 at 42/1 Worakham Phiphit Road in the Bang Nak area, right in the centre of Narathiwat town · Its clear selling point is that it is new — the rooms, furniture and bathrooms still feel fresh, without the wear you see in many of the town's older hotels · It is within walking distance of restaurants and convenience stores, and about 10 minutes by car from Narathiwat Airport, so it works for fly-in guests and self-drivers alike.

Rooms are air-conditioned, with both king and twin layouts · Each has a flat-screen TV, fridge, minibar, kettle and en-suite bathroom, and some come with a private balcony · What guests agree on is that the rooms are very clean, the beds are soft and the design is cute, clearly more thought-through than other hotels at a similar price in town · The one note is that some reviews say the balcony does not get the same cleaning attention as the room, so balcony fans may want to check theirs first.

"The room was great — very clean, comfortable and well looked after, with a soft bed and a cute design · The parking was nice and wide and easy to use, and the lobby and housekeeping staff were really friendly and helpful · There are restaurants and convenience stores just a short walk away."

What sets Pacinn apart from the usual town hotels is the Japanese / sushi restaurant on the ground floor · In a town where Japanese food is still hard to find, having a restaurant in the hotel itself is something many guests like — you can head down for dinner without going anywhere · There is also a breakfast service, free parking that reviews praise as wide and easy to use, and free Wi-Fi in every room.

Honestly, the thing to weigh up is night-time service · One review noted that the night staff and security felt less professional than the daytime team — a minority voice, but worth knowing · The other point is that the hotel is brand new, so review numbers are still small (around 6 on Trip.com), which means the 9.7 comes from a tiny base · It remains to be seen how consistent quality stays once guest numbers grow.

A tip from reading the reviews: if you want quiet, ask for a higher floor away from the street, as one review mentioned hearing dogs barking from lower street-facing rooms · Standard rooms run roughly ฿850–฿1,600/night depending on season and platform, so compare a few sites before booking · Overall, Pacinn is a sensible pick for anyone who wants a crisp, clean room in the centre of town at an affordable price, without staying in an older hotel.

honestSummary: Pacinn Narathiwat sells newness, clean rooms, a cute design, a central location and free parking at an affordable price — ideal for anyone who wants a brand-new room in the centre of Narathiwat, with an in-house Japanese restaurant as a bonus · The trade-offs are that it is newly opened, has few reviews, and night-time service is not yet settled.
honestChecks: If you expect professional service around the clock — one review found the night team less settled than daytime → handle anything important during the day and keep expectations measured for late hours.
If you are a light sleeper sensitive to noise — lower street-facing rooms can pick up outside noise, including dogs barking → ask for a higher floor away from the street when booking.
If you need full facilities like a pool or gym — this hotel focuses on rooms and the restaurant, with no pool → consider a hotel with more facilities if you need them.

faq.q: Where is Pacinn Narathiwat and what is nearby?
faq.a: Pacinn Narathiwat is at 42/1 Worakham Phiphit Road, Bang Nak, in central Narathiwat · Restaurants and convenience stores are within a short walk · The Clock Tower and town market are about 4-5 minutes by car · Narathat Beach and the Central Mosque are around 6-7 minutes by car · Narathiwat Airport (NAW) is about 10 minutes by car.

faq.q: How much does Pacinn Narathiwat cost and what rooms are available?
faq.a: Rates start from about ฿850/night for a standard room · There are king and twin layouts, and some rooms have a balcony, with prices rising to roughly ฿1,200–฿1,600 for larger or balcony rooms · Prices vary by season and platform, so compare a few sites before booking.

faq.q: Is the hotel really new, and what are the rooms like?
faq.a: Yes — Pacinn is a new hotel that opened in 2025 · Many guests praise the rooms as clean and fresh, with soft beds and a cute design · Each room has a flat-screen TV, fridge, minibar, kettle and en-suite bathroom, and some have a balcony · One note is that some reviews say the balcony is not cleaned as thoroughly as the room.

faq.q: Does Pacinn Narathiwat have a restaurant and parking?
faq.a: Yes — there is a Japanese / sushi restaurant on the ground floor, which is rare in Narathiwat town, so you can head down for dinner · There is a breakfast service (included in some packages) · And there is free on-site parking that reviews praise as wide and easy to use, handy for self-drivers.

faq.q: Who is Pacinn Narathiwat best for?
faq.a: It suits anyone who wants a crisp, clean room in central Narathiwat at an affordable price and would rather not stay in an older hotel · Good for solo travellers, couples and self-drivers thanks to free parking · The in-house Japanese restaurant is a bonus for anyone who wants dinner in the hotel.

faq.q: What should I know before booking Pacinn Narathiwat?
faq.a: Know that this is a newly opened hotel with few reviews so far, so the 9.7 comes from a small base · One review found night-time service less settled than the daytime team · Lower street-facing rooms can pick up outside noise, so ask for a higher inner room · Compare a few platforms and book ahead during festivals.
